chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Zakariyya ibn Adam who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the drunkard, the child, the insane person, the one whose reason is overpowered, and the one who has not yet consummated the marriage, so he said: 'It is not valid.'

key_terms.اَلْمَغْلُوبِ عَلَى عَقْلِهِ: The one whose reason is overpowered

ai.seo_question: Is divorce valid for a drunkard or a child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that talaq is invalid (la yajuzu) for those lacking full legal capacity, including the drunkard, child, insane, and reason-overpowered, as well as the groom before consummation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that valid divorce requires both mental competence and the completion of the marital bond, distinguishing it from mere contractual validity.
